python3 -c "
import parse

# Test R8 - findall with case_sensitive using named field
r = parse.findall('{word:w}', 'Hello WORLD hello', case_sensitive=True)
print(f'R8 findall case_sensitive (w): {[(x.named.get(\"word\")) for x in r]}')

r = parse.findall('{word:w}', 'Hello WORLD hello', case_sensitive=False)
print(f'R8 findall case_insensitive (w): {[(x.named.get(\"word\")) for x in r]}')

# Also test with explicit Parser
p1 = parse.Parser('{word:w}', case_sensitive=True)
p2 = parse.Parser('{word:w}', case_sensitive=False)
print(f'P1 re flags: {p1._re_flags}')
print(f'P2 re flags: {p2._re_flags}')

# The issue is that {word:w} uses \\w+ which matches word chars
# Case sensitivity matters when comparing letters like A vs a
"
